items.description: North Sea coast at Bridlington - Harbour Road and Floral Pavilion
items.message:
High tides and forecast weather conditions are expected to cause flooding tomorrow morning. 
Flooding is expected from 04:00 to 06:30 on 28/10/2026. 
High astronomical tides and a large surge is expected. The wind direction is predominantly offshore, so the main risk is from higher than normal water levels. Locations most affected will be coastal roads, promenades and footpaths. 
We are closely monitoring the situation . 
Avoid coastal roads, footpaths and carparks, which may be flooded. Stay away from promenades where wave and spray overtopping is possible 
This message will be updated by 10:30PM on Tuesday 27 October or as the situation changes.

items.description: South Hayling and South Eastoke seafront
items.message:
High tides are expected to cause flooding on Wednesday.
Flooding is expected for 2 hours either side of Wednesday afternoon's tide at 12:21 on 28/10/2026.  
The weather increases tide table values by 0.22 m. Total forecast tide is 5.23 metres Chart Datum (2.50 mAOD) at Portsmouth. Light Westerly Force 3 wind. South Hayling beach (towards Eastoke) has been affected by previous storms. Water could push further up the beach than normal. Property at Eastoke corner, near the nature reserve, and at Southwood Road may flood. Overtopping of splash walls along the beach front may flood gardens. Beach huts at West Beach, near the Inn on the beach, may also be affected. Thursday's tide at 00:45 on 29/10/2026 is forecast to be 50 cm lower (2 mAOD).
We are liaising with emergency services and local authorities .
Activate any flood protection products you may have.  
This message will be updated by 4:00PM on Wednesday 28 October or as the situation changes.

High tides on Wednesday may lead to flooding.
Flooding is possible for 2 hours either side of Wednesday's early morning tide at 00:00 on 28/10/2026.
The weather increases tide table values by 0.1 m. Total forecast tide is 6.05 metres Chart Datum (3.00 mAOD) at Littlehampton. Strong Westerly Force 5 wind. Waves could cause overtopping of the beach, affecting Climping Street Car Park. A small amount of water may then flow or be directed westwards along Mill Lane towards residential property in Climping Street. Wednesday's afternoon tide at 12:15 on 28/10/2026 is forecast to be 23 cm higher (3.23 mAOD). Flood impacts should reduce on Thursday.
We are closely monitoring the situation We routinely check the condition of the beach at Climping.
Consider activating any flood protection products you may have. Access could be restricted. Take care if visiting Climping beach.
This message will be updated by 6:00PM on Wednesday 28 October or as the situation changes.

High tides and forecast weather conditions tomorrow morning may lead to flooding.
Flooding is possible from 04:00 to 06:30 on 28/10/2026.
High astronomical tides and a large surge is expected. The wind direction is predominantly offshore, so the main risk is from higher than normal water levels. Locations most affected will be coastal roads, promenades and footpaths.
We are closely monitoring the situation.
Avoid coastal roads, footpaths and carparks, which may be flooded. Stay away from promenades where overtopping is possible.
This message will be updated by 11PM on Tuesday 27 October or as the situation changes.

There is no longer a threat of flooding.
The previous tide of concern has now passed,  the weather is more settled and no flooding is expected. High tide tomorrow morning may see this alert re-issued.
We will continue to monitor the situation and will issue further alerts or warnings if necessary. 
Continue to take care on waterside roads and footpaths and don't put yourself in unnecessary danger.

items.description: Severn estuary from Gloucester to Sharpness
items.message:
There is no longer a threat of flooding.
Coastal conditions are expected to improve and no flooding is expected.  
We will continue to monitor the situation and will issue further alerts or warnings if necessary.  
Continue to take care on waterside roads and footpaths and don't put yourself in unnecessary danger.
